newsitem.title: USA: Missile reports won't affect talks-Indian official.
newsitem.headline: Missile reports won't affect talks-Indian official.

text.p: Recent reports that India had moved medium-range ballistic missiles to its border with Pakistan would not affect upcoming talks between the two countries, Indian officials said here on Friday.

Indian and U.S. officials agreed that "the Prithvi leak was handled very well by both...Pakistan and India, and it will not have any effect on the talks," Indian Cabinet Secretary T.S.R. Subramanian said at a news conference.
Newspaper reports this week sparked denials by India that it had deployed Prithvi missiles aimed at Pakistan.
The Hindu newspaper said the Indian army had stored, but not deployed, Prithvi missiles near its border with Pakistan.

Last week, the Washington Post cited U.S. intelligence saying that India had moved fewer than a dozen Prithvi missiles, which can carry conventional but not nuclear warheads, to a prospective launch site near the border.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since independence in 1947. The neighbours are set to resume diplomatic talks next week.

In talks this week, U.S. and Indian officials said they would urge Pakistan to sign a global chemical weapons convention which the United States and India have already signed, according to Subramanian.
The officials, here with a trade mission, invited President Bill Clinton to join in India's celebration of 50 years of independence on August 15 or anytime during the year-long festivities.
"We got the impression that they were willing to look at it and come back to us," Subramanian said.
